name: Complete Sports and Management India Limited
sector: Amusement equipment distribution and entertainment centres
summary: Established amusement-equipment distributor with concentrated customers and weak cash conversion. IPO deployment and new venues remain assumption-sensitive; downside requires uncommitted financing.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Watchlist only, with inadequate price protection under the reference case. CSML has a long-standing amusement-equipment distribution franchise, but customer/principal concentration, weak collections and a shift into assembly and owned entertainment venues raise the capital requirement. The dated ₹181.50 price produces roughly 6.6% base annualized return against a 15% hurdle, not a compelling margin of safety. A successful bull case can work, while severe cash/ramp stress can eliminate equity. Scores are conditional estimates, not a buy or execution instruction.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026: Complete Sports and Management India Limited, ISIN INE2K6801014, BSE SME 544900. The original BSE notice admits trading on 4 September; the official interoperable master date 7 September is not substituted for that primary listing date. The master supports 20,560,000 shares and a 1,000-share lot. The secondary 19 October close is ₹181.50, giving ₹373.164 crore equity value and a ₹181,500 lot, not a live quote. Historical financial factors use standalone FY24–26; group figures remain separately labelled. Five-year terminal date is 19 October 2031, with FY27–31 annual forecasts plus a 202/365.25 FY32 stub. March balances and intervening IPO/borrowing assumptions roll forward to the valuation date; no claim is made that an October balance sheet has been observed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.02, GQS 5.0 after persistent cash-conversion cap 5, conditional IAS 3.655. R/D/P/L2/4/3/6. Full weights and raw/capped arithmetic retained; no missing-factor renormalization. GOV 4 / MOAT 6 / REV 6 / DUR 6 / CAP 5 / CASH 3 / BAL 5 / EXEC 5 / EARN 5 remain medium-confidence judgments. CASH 3 is persistent because three-year after-interest conversion is slightly negative, capping growth quality. BAL falls from 6 to 5 after including all opening claims and retaining non-ICICI debt. The base return spread maps to R 2; limited IPO/venue-cost variations do not change that band. L 6 is provisional rather than a fabricated 60-day measure. A one-point R change moves IAS 0.35; small composite differences are not precise rankings of future outcomes.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: CSML sources, distributes, installs and commissions bowling, arcade, go-karting and other amusement systems, with maintenance and management/consulting services. It is not an established nationwide venue chain. FY26 standalone product sales were ₹103.8619 crore and services ₹9.6983 crore. Brunswick bowling alone contributed ₹57.0135 crore. The Singapore subsidiary and 30.60% Synnccit associate are not gross-consolidated into the parent-only valuation. The proposed Bhiwandi assembly/equipment program and Duckpin venues introduce utilization, rent, food-and-beverage, safety and footfall risks beyond equipment distribution.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The Brunswick relationship dates to 2010, with Singapore/Malaysia/Indonesia territories added in August 2025. Technical installation, spares and an installed base provide differentiated access but not perpetual exclusivity. Top-ten suppliers represented 81.93% of purchases; the two largest customers TORQ03 and Malpani Arcade represented 48.83% of sales. A principal or large-customer loss would therefore matter disproportionately. Wonderla is a useful, non-identical venue diagnostic: its FY26 consolidated total income ₹551.079 crore, issuer-defined EBITDA ₹192.455 crore and 32.19 lakh visitors represent mature park/hospitality economics. Its PAT ₹81.734 crore also compares with a prior year containing ₹24.08 crore favorable deferred tax. Those margins, tax effects and asset intensity are not transferred to CSML, and no unverified current peer multiple is used.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Standalone FY24/FY25/FY26 revenue ₹81.5042/₹110.3457/₹113.5602 crore gives 18.0% two-year CAGR, but latest growth slowed to 2.9%. REV 6 is the 15–20% anchor 7 less one for that deceleration, constrained by only three verified comparable years. PAT ₹10.1176/₹11.4094/₹17.9532 crore grew faster than sales; operating margin and other income must therefore be distinguished. FY26 group revenue ₹117.0934 crore and PAT ₹18.1835 crore are diagnostics, not substituted into the standalone series. September 21 ₹24 crore go-karting and September 30 ₹40 crore family-entertainment releases involve unnamed South India customers; distinctness, execution timing and overlap are not independently established. They are not automatically added as ₹64 crore incremental sales or cash. The September 25 trial order has no disclosed value.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The RHP budgets ₹39.8824 crore for Bhiwandi equipment/assembly and ₹8.0905 crore for a new Duckpin, totaling ₹47.9729 crore over FY27–28, plus ₹11.5 crore debt repayment. The new venue site was not yet identified; deposits, advance rent and some taxes/incidental costs come from internal funds. Existing Duckpin Malad opened 24 July after the March accounts, and All Sett Go also adds hospitality exposure. Malad/All Sett Go monthly rents ₹0.097/₹0.06513 crore total ₹1.94556 crore annually before any new outlet. Model margins are after rent, so no duplicate lease-debt subtraction is made. The reference assumes legacy 10% growth and 19% margin, new assembly revenue 0/12/25/40/50 crore in FY27–31 at 16% margin, and venue revenue 6/14/20/23/25 at 15%. These are scenarios, not guidance or booked orders. Incremental venue cash ₹8 crore and incidental cash ₹3 crore are bounded by separate sensitivities because actual post-March expenditure is unavailable.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY26 director remuneration was ₹2.25 crore versus ₹0.8491 crore, with an additional ₹0.8595 crore commission to Rohit Mathur. Synccit software charges were ₹1.626 crore. A registered 31 March 2026 agreement covers the ₹2.57 crore residential-property purchase from the promoter; the entire ₹2.57 crore was already advanced by March, not an unpaid balance inferred from the ₹0.979 crore annual cash movement. Its business use and independent pricing merit scrutiny while collections are weak, but identifiable consideration is not evidence of diversion. The 28 May acquisition of 3,060 Synnccit shares at ₹7,500 each totals ₹2.295 crore, against ₹2.2865 crore earlier advances, leaving only ₹0.0085 crore conditional settlement. No duplicate full acquisition charge is imposed. These conflicts and compensation economics support GOV 4 without alleging proved abuse.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Standalone CFO ₹8.8328/−₹3.3277/−₹3.8209 crore sums to only 4.27% of PAT. Financing-classified cash interest ₹0.1995/₹0.5526/₹1.1146 crore takes cumulative owner cash conversion slightly below zero. FY26 receivables rose ₹35.6377 crore to ₹47.941 crore despite 2.9% sales growth; inventory released ₹14.0509 crore and loans/advances ₹12.3032 crore, insufficient to offset receivables and reduced customer/other liabilities. Management classifies receivables as good, including ₹5.7753 crore older than six months; this is not independent collection verification. Mechanical CFO less PPE/CWIP/capital-advance expenditure is−₹7.6901 crore before property cash and interest. FD release ₹2.5618 crore is financing of cash needs, not earnings. Core FY26 EBITDA ₹23.9193 crore removes all ₹1.6414 crore other income, including gratuity gain, balance write-offs and discounts, rather than assuming every item recurs. Group CFO−₹3.6478 crore and cash ₹0.9827 crore are not mixed into the parent bridge.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The funded model starts with March cash ₹0.5594 crore, debt ₹8.9859 crore and operating WC ₹42.5468 crore. Ordinary statutory, payroll, customer-advance and expense balances remain inside WC, including ₹0.4332 crore other provisions. Tax ₹5.9196 crore, current gratuity ₹0.072 crore, subsidiary due ₹0.3234 crore and associate residual ₹0.0085 crore settle once outside WC. No separately identified tax asset is invented. Long-term unfunded gratuity ₹0.3797 crore and refundable deposits ₹0.8385 crore remain terminal claims. The August ₹11.5606 crore figure is selected ICICI cash credit, not total debt: retaining March other debt gives a conditional ₹12.81 crore bridge before assumed ₹11.5 crore repayment. Incremental cash-credit proceeds ₹3.8241 crore help fund, rather than duplicate, the post-March cash uses.

Assumed upper-band IPO price ₹135 and 55.5 lakh new shares imply ₹74.925 crore gross, but final price/allotment and expenses were not primary-reconciled. The reference uses ₹7.5 crore expenses, hence ₹67.425 crore net, with lower-band ₹128 and ₹5.5–10 crore expense cases. Project cash is reserved and released only against expenditure; it is not freely available twice. Every case links WC, capex, depreciation, positive-profit tax, opening claims and financing. New draws incur half-year interest; the bridge and mandatory repayment have mid-year timing, ordinary excess-cash repayment year-end. Interest/tax/draw are solved jointly. Uncommitted new borrowing is a requirement, not available finance.

bear ₹68.53, -17.70% annualized, peak debt ₹28.89 crore; base ₹249.38, 6.56% annualized, peak debt ₹13.07 crore; bull ₹529.36, 23.87% annualized, peak debt ₹12.81 crore; severe ₹0.00, -100.00% annualized, peak debt ₹67.69 crore. The base 15% hurdle entry is ₹123.99;12%/18% entries are ₹141.51/₹109.01. The 6x terminal sensitivity is approximately flat-to-negative annual return;12x alone remains below 15%. A 20% equity raise adds both cash and shares. FD/property recoveries, collection losses, WC 50%, project overrun and delayed ramp all rerun the funding model rather than merely change terminal arithmetic.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent-loss paths include a major principal/customer loss, collection failure after delivery, imported equipment becoming slow-moving, unsuccessful assembly qualification and loss-making leased venues. A 10% receivable noncollection stress consumes ₹4.7941 crore; it is a sensitivity, not an expected provision. The bear case requires debt above the disclosed ₹18 crore ICICI sanction, while severe stress produces no terminal equity. The reference does not assume the IPO eliminates every liability or that deposits/property can be liquidated at book value. Counterevidence is meaningful: equity capital, identifiable assets and a long distribution history can support survival, and base operations repay debt. Those positives do not establish adverse-case financing or protect a high entry valuation.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At ₹181.50, fivefold and tenfold targets are ₹907.50 and ₹1,815. With 20.56 million unchanged shares these require ₹1,865.82/₹3,731.64 crore equity. At 9x and roughly base terminal net cash/claims, the implied annual EBITDA requirement is far above the approximately ₹49.33 crore base. Ignoring net cash entirely gives ₹207.31/₹414.63 crore EBITDA; at 20% operating margin that is roughly ₹1,037/₹2,073 crore revenue, versus FY26 ₹113.56 crore. These reverse tests imply about 38%/59% annual value growth before dilution. Even the linked bull falls short of 5x. A multiple-only re-rating or unsupported repetition of announced orders is not a credible bridge to those outcomes.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First obtain final allotment/prospectus, actual IPO expenses and monitored use, with current cash-credit/other-debt balances. Reconcile customer-by-customer collections and supplier/customer advances, including the two large September releases and their overlap/timing. Track new-venue footfall, revenue per visitor, margins after rent and cash maintenance, and distinguish assembly orders from trials. Monitor property use, associate returns, related-party terms and compensation. For trading, the 29 observed secondary sessions yield lower-bound mean/median ₹1.365/₹0.713 crore and theoretical 5% exit 1.40 days for ₹5 lakh; the latest 20 imply 1.82 days. A ₹181,500 lot is 36.3% of that reference position. The missing September 4 observation is unknown, not a zero, and no 60-session claim is made. Check BSE-specific surveillance, circuits, spreads and depth before any executable decision.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Conditional watchlist with weak price protection, not a compounder classification. The franchise merits continued monitoring, but recent earnings quality and unproven reinvestment do not justify assuming the bull case. The numeric conditional IAS is low because the base return misses the hurdle and downside is funding-sensitive; it is not an allegation of issuer default or fraud. A materially lower valuation, sustained cash recovery and source-verified project/IPO deployment would be more relevant than cosmetic score movement. Position sizing is not prescribed from turnover proxies alone.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The original 481-page RHP was read in relevant business, financial, opening-claim, debt, objects and related-party sections; original September issuer releases and the BSE listing notice are retained with mirror provenance. Refreshed issuer IPO/annual/shareholding pages and targeted searches did not yield the final prospectus or actual post-IPO cash deployment. That absence is a research limit, not proof the issuer failed to publish. Three audited comparable years are verified; older private-company accounts are not invented. The Wonderla release supplies a primary, explicitly non-identical peer diagnostic. Price/history are labelled secondary. IPO price/expenses, post-March venue costs, ramp, margin, WC, multiple, recoveries and future funding are assumptions with full linked sensitivities. No forecast is presented as a guarantee, and no court or surveillance clearance is inferred from an absent record.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Conditional estimated scores, not executable advice; cash cap and dated secondary-price/funding bounds explicit.

GOV.reason: Promoter property/share purchases and compensation step-up require strong conflict controls, particularly while cash conversion is weak. Contrary evidence: registered property agreement and completed share transfer disclose identifiable consideration; no diversion or criminal abuse is established.

MOAT.reason: Fifteen-year Brunswick relationship, exclusive territories and installation/maintenance expertise create differentiated access. Contrary evidence: half of revenue depends on one principal and customers are concentrated; exclusivity can change and is not a perpetual franchise.

REV.reason: Two-year standalone CAGR about 18.0% maps to 7; subtract one for latest-year growth only 2.9%. Short history and lack of five-year audited comparables constrain confidence. September orders are positive contrary evidence but not booked revenue or a justification for retroactive organic-growth inflation.

DUR.reason: Installed-base service and distribution relationships provide recurring elements. Contrary evidence: customers depend on discretionary venue capex, new owned outlets add footfall/lease risk, and trial orders are unproven.

CAP.reason: Historically low equipment capex supported profit, but IPO-funded ₹47.97 crore project plan and promoter-linked capital uses materially alter the asset base. Contrary evidence: clear project budgets and debt-repayment allocation support financeability; future returns are not established.

CASH.reason: Three-year reported CFO/PAT is only 4.27%; deduct financing-classified cash interest and it is slightly negative. Two negative operating-cash years, receivable growth and new fixed costs support a persistent cash cap. Contrary evidence: FY24 was cash-positive and collection/advances can reverse; no assumption all receivables are lost.

BAL.reason: Fresh equity can fund specified projects and selected cash-credit repayment, but March tax/employee claims, retained other debt, post-March venues and WC consume funds. The base peak is manageable only conditionally; bear requirements exceed the disclosed ₹18 crore ICICI line. Contrary evidence: the gross equity issue and identifiable project/debt budgets materially improve funding capacity; no established default.

EXEC.reason: Territory expansion, operating outlet launch and announced project wins show activity. Contrary evidence: large receivable build, equipment assembly and owned-outlet economics remain unproven; announcements are not cash execution.

EARN.reason: PAT grew much faster than nearly flat revenue and receivables, making margin/collection normalization material. Contrary evidence: supplier/purchase mix and distribution margin can genuinely improve profitability; no unsupported revenue-fraud finding.

R.reason: At ₹181.50 the conditional base five-year IRR is approximately 6.6%, about 8.4 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, mapping to 2. Lower IPO price,5.5–10 crore issue expenses and 4–12 crore existing-venue cash ranges independently remain in this return band. These bounds justify medium conditional confidence, not verified current net cash. Stronger operating/multiple assumptions yield materially more; severe stress can eliminate equity.

D.reason: Bear terminal equity suffers material impairment and needs borrowing beyond the disclosed ICICI facility; severe stress wipes modeled equity. Opening claims and project cash are not ignored. Contrary evidence: the base retires debt and retains cash, and fresh equity/asset recovery can cushion stress, but no committed adverse-case recapitalization is established.

P.reason: The dated price fails the 15% hurdle under the base and even the isolated 12x terminal sensitivity; the base 15% hurdle entry is approximately ₹124 rather than ₹181.50. Contrary evidence: the combined bull operating and multiple case exceeds the hurdle, so this is insufficient protection at this price, not a claim the business has no value.

L.reason: Observed 20/29-session low-turnover bounds imply 1.82/1.40 days at 5% participation, raw 9. Deduct 2 for the ₹181,500 lot consuming 36.3% of a ₹5 lakh reference and 1 for short secondary-only history/missing first session and unknown live depth. This is provisional capacity, not verified 60-session liquidity or BSE surveillance clearance.

confidence.uncertainty: Material scenario and execution uncertainty; no probabilities assigned.

gates.reason: Identifiable disclosed related-party property/share purchases and compensation require minority scrutiny; no proved diversion or critical shareholder abuse established.
